picks.why: Only candidate. It reads at once as a cowboy hat: chunky soft-plastic shape, warm leather tone, simple band, no extra props.
Shaft-to-foot proportions look like a real boot, and the stitched shaft says cowboy boot right away. Candidate 2's shaft is stretched too tall.
Only candidate. The coil plus open loop reads as a lasso, it fills the frame well, and nothing extra is added.
Centered and well framed, with the two batwing halves even. In candidate 1 the left door sits higher than the right, and candidate 2 is shoved off to the left.
The tilted 3/4 pose matches the real cards, which are angled rather than flat. Candidate 1 is a flat, head-on icon, the staging the lessons flag as generated.
Biggest and centered, so the cactus fills the frame the way real hero objects do. Candidate 2 sits off-center and candidate 3 is smaller.
The saddle is larger and gently angled, filling the card like the real computer card. Candidates 1 and 3 are flatter, and the horn in 1 is stretched.
Only candidate. A simple hooped barrel with honest proportions and a plain plank floor, no invented extras.
Only candidate. The canvas cover, spoked wheels and tongue read as a covered wagon. It is a bit stubby, but nothing is invented.
Only candidate. Smokestack, cowcatcher, red wheels and tender read instantly as an old steam train, staged at a 3/4 angle on track.
